newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile copper concentrate output seen climbing.
newsitem.headline: Chile copper concentrate output seen climbing.

text.p: Chile's production of copper in concentrates will rise by one million tonnes to over three million tonnes by the end of the decade as the result of new mines and expansion of existing pits, said copper analysts.

"National production of copper concentrates will show an important growth in coming years as the result of the maturing of different development projects and important expansion programs," said a report from state studies center Comision Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco).
Copper in concentrate production totalled 2.09 million tonnes last year and will rise to 3.08 million tonnes by 2000, said the report.

Projects coming on stream include an expansion at the huge Escondida copper mine, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp Plc and the development of the Los Pelambres pit which belongs to Chile's Luksic group.
The growth in concentrate output will far outstrip expansion plans at Chile's seven smelters where capacity will rise by just eight percent by 2000, said Cochilco.
South Korean industrial giant Hyundai has said it is studying building a smelter in Chile.
Cochilco figures showed Chile will have 1.2 million tonnes of copper in concentrates in 2000 which are not subject to long term supply contracts and could supply a new smelter.

Although more than 40 percent of concentrates not processed in Chile are shipped abroad under long-term contracts to finance new mines, the surplus should attract the attention of investors, said the report.
"The availability of concentrates will be more than enough to generate interest in expanding existing facilities...as well as the development of new smelters," it said.
Local smelter Refimet, owned by Chilean and Canadian firms, has already announced plans to boost output by 140,000 tonnes to 300,000 tonnes a year.
